title: PIM for Active Directory: deploy the hybrid worker (Azure VM or on-premises with Azure Arc)
purpose: Deploys the PIM for Active Directory hybrid worker in the right order, step by step, and remembers where it got to so it can stop for the Active Directory step and continue later.
whenToRun: Once per hybrid worker, when you start using PIM for Active Directory: -Target Azure builds a new Azure VM for it, -Target Arc uses your own on-premises Windows server that is already Azure Arc-enabled and domain-joined. Run it first without -Apply to see the plan, then with -Apply; it stops for the Active Directory step (and, when a new KDS root key was created, for the ~10 hours that key needs) and continues with -Resume -Apply.

runAs.name: Contributor (or Owner)
runAs.scope: -Target Azure: the subscription or the worker's resource group, and Network Contributor on the networks it peers with; -Target Arc: Reader on the Arc machine and the Azure Connected Machine Resource Administrator role (run-command) on it
runAs.why: creates the worker's network and VM (Azure), reads the Arc machine and runs the install on it through run-command

runAs.name: User Access Administrator (or Role Based Access Control Administrator)
runAs.why: grants the worker's identity Storage Blob Data Reader on the container that holds the PIM code

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: grants the worker's identity the Graph application roles Group.Read.All, User.Read.All and PrivilegedAssignmentSchedule.Read.AzureADGroup (read only)

runAs.name: Microsoft Entra admin of the PIM SQL server (or a member of its admin group)
runAs.why: creates the worker's contained database user (db_datareader + db_datawriter). Run the script in Windows PowerShell 5.1 for this step.

runAs.name: Active Directory: an account that may create gMSAs, groups, GPOs and OU permissions (on a domain controller)
runAs.scope: the domain -- the AD step only, which this script PRINTS and the AD administrator runs
runAs.why: the worker writes AD only as group managed service accounts, which the AD step creates with their least-privilege rights

changes.object: resource group, VNet + subnet, deny-all-inbound NSG, NAT gateway egress, peerings to -PeerVnetId, the worker VM with a system-assigned identity and no public IP, a SQL VNet rule (New-PimHybridWorkerInfra.ps1)
changes.why: the worker's own isolated network and machine
changes.undo: delete the resource group and the peerings on the remote networks

changes.object: one firewall rule per on-premises egress address
changes.why: lets the on-premises worker reach a public SQL endpoint; not needed with a private endpoint

changes.object: Install-PimHybridWorker.ps1 through run-command: domain join (Azure only), PowerShell 7, the gMSAs installed and tested, log on as a batch job for them, C:\PIM locked down, the PIM code, six scheduled tasks; on Arc the gMSAs join the local group 'Hybrid agent extension applications'
changes.undo: delete the scheduled tasks 'PIM Hybrid *' and C:\PIM; remove the gMSAs from the local group

changes.why: the worker reads the PIM groups and who is active in them; it never writes to Entra
changes.undo: remove the app role assignments from the identity's enterprise application

changes.why: the worker updates itself with its identity -- no SAS, no PAT

changes.object: a contained user (-SqlUserName) created from the identity
changes.why: the worker reads its work and writes its state and audit

parameters.name: Target
parameters.help: Azure (a new Azure VM) or Arc (your own Azure Arc-enabled on-premises server). Not needed with -Resume.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The subscription of the worker (Azure) or of the Arc machine.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant. The REST session is pinned to it and every step refuses another.

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the worker's resource group.

parameters.name: Location
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the region.

parameters.name: VmName
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the VM and computer name (max 15 characters).

parameters.name: VmSize
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the VM size.

parameters.name: VnetName
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the worker's VNet.

parameters.name: AddressPrefix
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the VNet address space.

parameters.name: SubnetPrefix
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the worker subnet.

parameters.name: PeerVnetId
parameters.help: -Target Azure (required there): the VNet resource ids to peer with -- the network with the domain controllers, optionally the PIM environment's.

parameters.name: DnsServers
parameters.help: -Target Azure (required there): the domain controllers' addresses (the VNet DNS).

parameters.name: Egress
parameters.help: -Target Azure: NatGateway, or None when your network already routes outbound. Never a public IP on the VM.

parameters.name: UseRemoteGateways
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the DCs are reached through the hub's VPN / ExpressRoute gateway (with -GatewayVnetId). Passed to the infra step.

parameters.name: GatewayVnetId
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the hub VNet with the gateway (one of -PeerVnetId).

parameters.name: AllowForwardedTraffic
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the worker-side peering(s) accept traffic the hub forwards.

parameters.name: PrivateSqlDnsZoneId
parameters.help: A private-only PIM database: the existing privatelink.database.windows.net zone, linked to the worker VNet; the DCs' DNS forwarder is printed.

parameters.name: PrivateDnsLinkVnetId
parameters.help: More VNets to link the zone to (the DCs' VNet when they are Azure VMs; the DNS Private Resolver's VNet).

parameters.name: CreatePrivateDnsZone
parameters.help: Create the standard privatelink.database.windows.net zone only when it is missing.

parameters.name: PrivateDnsZoneResourceGroup
parameters.help: Where the standard zone lives, instead of -PrivateSqlDnsZoneId.

parameters.name: PrivateSql
parameters.help: Print the conditional forwarder for a private-only database (implied by the zone options).

parameters.name: DnsForwarderIp
parameters.help: The address the printed forwarder points at (168.63.129.16 for DCs in Azure; a Private Resolver inbound endpoint for DCs on-premises).

parameters.name: ArcMachineResourceId
parameters.help: -Target Arc (required there): /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines/<server>.

parameters.name: SqlAllowedPublicIp
parameters.help: -Target Arc with a public SQL endpoint: your on-premises egress address(es); one firewall rule each. Leave empty with a private endpoint.

parameters.name: SqlServerId
parameters.help: The PIM SQL server's resource id.

parameters.name: SqlDatabase
parameters.help: The PIM database.

parameters.name: SqlUserName
parameters.help: The worker's contained database user. Name it per worker when you run more than one.

parameters.name: SourceContainerId
parameters.help: The resource id of the blob container with the PIM code (pim-src-<version>.tar.gz + channel.json).

parameters.name: Ring
parameters.help: The update ring this environment follows (or -Version).

parameters.name: Version
parameters.help: Pin a version instead of following a ring.

parameters.name: GrantMailSend
parameters.help: Also grant Graph Mail.Send, so new AD admin accounts get their initial password by mail.

parameters.name: PlanOnly
parameters.help: Install the worker in plan-only mode: every run plans and logs, nothing is written to AD until Configure is re-run without it.

parameters.name: AdDomain
parameters.help: The domain's NetBIOS name (the gMSAs are DOMAIN\name).

parameters.name: WorkerComputerName
parameters.help: The worker's computer name in AD.

parameters.name: ComputerOu
parameters.help: The OU of the worker's computer account (printed into the AD command).

parameters.name: GmsaName
parameters.help: The Tier-0 worker identity.

parameters.name: GmsaOu
parameters.help: The OU for the gMSAs and their groups.

parameters.name: GroupsOu
parameters.help: The OU where PIM for AD creates its groups.

parameters.name: AdminAccountsOu
parameters.help: The OU(s) of the AD admin accounts PIM creates.

parameters.name: ServerGmsaName
parameters.help: The separate Tier-1 identity for server onboarding (e.g. gMSA-PIM-L2-T1); needs -ServerOu.

parameters.name: ServerOu
parameters.help: The servers OU(s) whose local Administrators get the server identity (a GPO). Keep the worker itself out of it.

parameters.name: GrantProtectedGroupMembership
parameters.help: Let the worker change the members of protected groups (AdminSDHolder) -- Tier 0.

parameters.name: CreateKdsRootKey
parameters.help: Let the AD step create the forest's KDS root key when there is none; the run then waits ~10 hours before Configure.

parameters.name: AdServer
parameters.help: A specific domain controller for the worker's AD calls.

parameters.name: Apply
parameters.help: Run the steps. Without it the script prints the plan only.

parameters.name: Resume
parameters.help: Continue from the state file; every value given on the first run is remembered.

parameters.name: StatePath
parameters.help: The state file to use.

parameters.name: KdsRootKeyCreatedUtc
parameters.help: When the AD step created a new KDS root key (it prints the time): Configure waits until it is ~10 hours old.

parameters.name: OdjBlob
parameters.help: -Target Azure: the offline domain-join blob the AD step printed (never stored in the state file).

parameters.name: OdjBlobFile
parameters.help: -Target Azure: a file holding that blob.

parameters.name: PrintOnly
parameters.help: Do not use run-command: write the self-contained install script for the server administrator to run locally.

parameters.name: JoinRebootWaitSeconds
parameters.help: -Target Azure: how long to wait for the reboot after the domain join.

readsOnly: the subscription (its tenant, checked against -TenantId) and, for -Target Arc, the Arc machine (status, OS, identity)
the state file of an earlier run (-Resume)
the run-command result (state, exit code, output) of each install phase
network: management.azure.com (ARM), graph.microsoft.com, login.microsoftonline.com, the PIM SQL server (1433) for the grant step
nothing to the worker machine directly: the install reaches it through Azure run-command (outbound from the machine's agent)
whatIf: Prints the plan: every step in order with what it would create or grant and the exact Active Directory command, plus the state file it would use. Nothing is changed, nothing is called, no state file is written. -Apply runs it.
undo: Remove-PimHybridWorker.ps1 removes it all (plan first, -Apply). By hand: -Target Azure: delete the worker's resource group and the peerings on the remote networks. Both targets: remove the worker identity's Graph app roles, its Storage Blob Data Reader assignment and its database user (DROP USER); on the server delete the 'PIM Hybrid *' scheduled tasks and C:\PIM; in AD delete the gMSAs and their groups (Initialize-PimHybridWorkerAd.ps1 created them) and the servers GPO.
